chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Ash'ari, from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had fever, so Jibreel (peace be upon him) came to him and gave him a charm (ruqyah), and he said: 'In the name of Allah, I perform ruqyah on you, O Muhammad, and in the name of Allah, I heal you, and in the name of Allah, from every disease that exhausts you, in the name of Allah, and Allah is your Healer. In the name of Allah, take it, so be happy with it. In the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Kind,
So I swear by the places of the stars
You will surely be cured by the permission of Allah
Bakr said: And I asked him about the ruqyah for fever, so he narrated this to me.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruqyah (spiritual healing) prescribed for fever in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi records the specific ruqyah (spiritual healing) prescribed by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) for fever, rooted in the Prophet’s own experience and the revelation of Jibreel. It emphasizes the theological principle that healing is ultimately from Allah, using divine names as a means of seeking cure under His permission. The inclusion of the oath by the 'stations of the stars' (mawāqiʿ al-nujūm) links this physical remedy to cosmic signs, reflecting the Shia tradition of viewing illness and healing within a broader metaphysical framework.

en.hubeali: H 14536 – Al-Husayn Bin Muhammad Al-Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Is’haq Al-Ashary, from Bakr Bin Muhammad Al-Azady who said:

Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The Rasoolsaww Allahazwj had fever so Jibraeelas gave to himsaww a charm. So he said: ‘In the Name of Allahazwj I perform incantation on yousaww, O Muhammadsaww, and in the Name of Allahazwj I heal yousaww, and in the Name of Allahazwj from every disease which has exhausted yousaww, and in the Name of Allahazwj, and Allahazwj is yoursaww Healer. So take it and congratulations to yousaww.
[56:75] Nay, I swear by the places of the stars
for it would free you<sup>saww</sup> from it by the Permission of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
Bakr (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked himasws about an incantation[13] for the fever, so heasws narrated to me with this’.
en.sarwar: 88. Al-Husayn Bin Muhammad Al-Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Is’haq Al-Ashary, from Bakr Bin Muhammad Al-Azady who said:

Abu Abdullah (a.s.) said: ‘The Rasool (saww) Allah (azwj) had fever so Jibraeel (as) gave to him (saww) a charm. So he said: ‘In the Name of Allah (azwj) I perform incantation on you (saww), O Muhammad (saww), and in the Name of Allah (azwj) I heal you (saww), and in the Name of Allah (azwj) from every disease which has exhausted you (saww), and in the Name of Allah (azwj), and Allah (azwj) is your (saww) Healer. So take it and congratulations to you (saww).
Nay, I swear by the places of the stars for it would free you (saww) from it by the Permission of Allah (azwj)’.
Bakr (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him (a.s.) about an incantation for the fever, so he (a.s.) narrated to me with this’.
